title: Prioritize complete-job data movement and useful parallelism after cross-tool comparison
question: Where does current Chopper leave split/shuffle throughput on the table against DuckDB and qsv?
summary: qsv and qsvlite lead balanced splitting; DuckDB leads the measured external shuffle; Chopper beats naive DuckDB balanced output. Investigate admitted batching and avoidable Run payload passes before changing sorting kernels.

workloads: 128 MiB repeated and varied four-text-column CSVs; 2 GiB repeated input; eight consecutive balanced outputs and full shuffle followed by balanced output.

validation.summary: 69 measured complete jobs and 23 excluded warmups across six cohorts independently verify fields, unique IDs, quotas and balanced order; separate smoke, failed DuckDB256MiB OOM, nondivisible quota and component/profile diagnostics remain distinct.

limitations: Warm WSL2/ext4 with 62 GiB host RAM; forced engine spill does not reproduce physical-RAM exhaustion, 40 GiB cold storage, native Windows or hosted behavior.
Three observations per cell; small varied-shuffle ranges overlap. No general ranking or tail claim.
qsv random sort is resident and unconstrained. Memory settings are not RSS caps; qsv count uses a separate Polars pool.
DuckDB adapter uses fixture-specific absent NULL sentinel and materializes/counts/exports LIMIT-OFFSET ranges; not an optimal or general text backend.
Component probes are not causal whole-job ablations; returned Chopper temporary counters precede publication.
exclusions: All warmups, smoke runs, failed/setup attempts and instrumented component/CTAS diagnostics are excluded from complete-job medians.
Different fixtures, builds, cohorts and prior historical/user-supplied percentages are not pooled.
reopen_when: A narrowly scoped candidate eliminates a demonstrated pass or row-handling cost, preserves contracts and passes a frozen complete-job decision rule; do not restore rejected radix, buckets, copied parser or adaptive FY unchanged.
